brief.topic: Reading a Hill Before Taking a Step

s01: A hill can become a drawing without losing its heights.
Each of these lines follows one level.
Imagine slicing the hill at evenly spaced heights.
Those slices become a contour map.
Walk along one contour, and your height stays the same.
At this point, that direction lies along the tangent.
The steepest uphill direction points across it, at a right angle.
This arrow is called the gradient.
It describes the fastest increase in height per small step on the map.
Closer contours mean the same rise happens over less ground.
Move to another part of the hill.
The uphill direction changes with the shape beneath you.
This is a local guide, not a promise of the best whole route.
A quiet set of lines lets us read a landscape before taking a step.

scenes.narration:
A hill can become a drawing without losing its heights. Each of these lines follows one level.

Imagine slicing the hill at evenly spaced heights. Now look straight down. Those slices become a contour map.

Walk along one contour, and your height stays the same. At this point, that direction lies along the tangent. The steepest uphill direction points across it, at a right angle.

This arrow is called the gradient. It describes the fastest increase in height per small step on the map. Closer contours mean the same rise happens over less ground.

Move to another part of the hill. The uphill direction changes with the shape beneath you. This is a local guide, not a promise of the best whole route. A quiet set of lines lets us read a landscape before taking a step.
